Execution order: step 11 of 13. Depends on Adashi task ID 20. Complete this prerequisite before starting.

Phase: shared server SQL implementation.

Implement the backend chosen in task 20 using the same shared storage interfaces:
- Add schema/migrations and CRUD/query support for all authoritative project domains, portable identities, links and history.
- Enforce project isolation and the chosen identity/authorization/attribution model.
- Implement atomic validation and guarded writes, resource-scoped conflicts, operationId replay and reference integrity using server transactions.
- Support independent concurrent users without a project-wide edit lock or last-write-wins behavior.
- Add bounded connections/timeouts, cancellation, reconnection and precise errors. Resolve an unknown commit result using durable operation receipts before retrying.
- Implement shared change detection so desktop and MCP observe other clients' committed changes without overwriting local drafts.
- Keep domain semantics in shared code; backend-specific SQL and driver types stay inside this adapter.

Acceptance: two independently authenticated clients using desktop/MCP can operate on one project through the server adapter. Disjoint writes succeed, overlapping writes return conflicts, retries do not duplicate changes, and one project's operations cannot read or alter another project.

Markdown design artefact integration (approved 2026-09-25):
Before finalizing the SQL adapter, complete the shared Markdown API, SQLite/text, migration and reference foundations through Markdown 05/12 (task ID 29; earlier steps are transitive prerequisites). Implement every Markdown snapshot/query/mutation/reference method behind the same storage adapter, with complete bodies, portable identities, ordered associations, bindings, task/QA links, search/backlinks and exact token/receipt semantics. Enforce project/user isolation and authorization. Test independent and conflicting edits, guarded referenced deletion, retry after lost commit response, no-op behavior and committed notifications. Do not return success from missing/default domain methods. Desktop/MCP consume the same stored documents; generated files remain local derived outputs.

data.title: Storage 11/13 — Implement the shared server SQL adapter and multi-user transactions
